title: Pollenless endeavour: loss of a glyoxal/galactose oxidase causes male sterility in rice
content: Seed plants reproduce through sexual reproduction by the male and female gametes produced in pollens and ovules, respectively. Viable pollens, vital for successful fertilization, are surrounded by an outer protective layer known as exine. The exine is deposited by the tapetum, an innermost somatic layer in the anthers in direct contact with developing pollens. The tapetum secretes nutrients such as sporopollenin, proteins, lipids, and enzymes through subsequent events including the programmed cell death (PCD) of specific target cells (Zhang et al. 2011; Walbot and Egger 2016). Timely degradation of the tapetum is critical for exine formation in developing pollens.
